en: Heating a sealed aerosol can causes the gas inside to expand, which can make the can explode and cause severe injuries.
Stirring powdered oral rehydration salts into clean drinking water creates a solution that replaces lost body fluids faster than drinking plain water.
Leaving cooked rice at room temperature allows bacteria to multiply rapidly, causing a chemical change that makes the food unsafe to eat.
Water expands when it freezes into solid ice, which can burst closed glass bottles left inside a household freezer.
Washing your hands with soap removes oily dirt and germs because soap molecules break down the lipids in the oil.
Mixing liquid bleach with acidic cleaners like vinegar produces toxic chlorine gas that can severely damage your lungs.
Rubbing liquid alcohol on your skin causes rapid evaporation, which absorbs heat from your body and lowers your skin temperature.
Shaking a liquid antibiotic suspension mixes the solid medicine particles evenly into the liquid so you get the correct dose.
Metals are good conductors of heat, so you must always use a dry pot holder when lifting a hot metal pan.
Chewing food into smaller pieces increases its surface area, allowing saliva to chemically break down starches faster for better digestion.
Pouring cold water into a hot glass container causes rapid contraction, which can shatter the glass and cause painful cuts.
Boiling water kills harmful bacteria, but filtering it through a clean cloth first removes solid dirt particles before you boil it.
